A different way to find the shape

Think in gestures.
Work with bones.

Some poses begin with a line of action, not an individual joint. BoneSculpt PRO lets you work across bone chains with a brush, then narrow the influence when the details need attention.

Your armature stays an armature. You’re editing pose transforms, with control over the bones, channels and local axes each brush can affect.

SCULPT / REFINE / REPEAT

A brush for
the whole chain.

Drag over the bones you want to pose. Adjust the radius, strength and falloff to move from a broad gesture to a local correction.

  • Choose your scope. Work on Selected bones or All visible bones within the brush.
  • Protect what’s settled. Mask bones and use connected-parent protection.
  • Keep your setup. Undo a completed stroke while retaining your current brush settings.

Optional PRO tools for working across

01 / MIRROR

Give both sides
some attention.

Sculpt existing left/right bone partners together. Choose the armature-space mirror axis and set the name pairs to match your rig.

Requires matching bone names. Check the paired side as you work.

02 / MESH COLLISION

Bring a surface
into the process.

Choose a mesh object or collection as a collider. Collision rotates eligible bones away from sampled surfaces with an adjustable clearance.

Requires Rotation and an enabled axis. Bone sampling is not full mesh collision or physics simulation.

03 / MESH ONION SKIN

Read the poses
around this one.

View evaluated mesh ghosts from earlier and later frames. Adjust their range, style and opacity to compare poses in the viewport.

Keyframe other animated edits before enabling or refreshing ghosts. The sampling limitation below applies to manual and automatic refreshes.

Open full-size clip ↗Animated image version ↗
!

Before you turn on onion skin

Sampling visits other frames and restores the active rig’s pose-bone transforms. Other unkeyed animated values—including object transforms, custom rig-control properties and shape keys—may reset to keyed values. Keyframe these changes before enabling or refreshing onion skin. Turning off Auto Update changes refresh timing, not this limitation.

05 / Put it to work

Small bones.
Expressive shapes.

Three starting points for bone-chain rigs.
Adapt the channels and masks to your setup.

01

Hair & strands

Select a group of chains. Mask the roots you want to hold, then use Grab for the silhouette. Curl adds a turn; Smooth relaxes directional kinks.

GRAB → CURL → SMOOTH
02

Tails & tendrils

Begin with a broad Grab stroke. Reduce the radius for the tip, add Twist where needed, and compare neighboring keyed poses with Tween.

GRAB → TWIST → TWEEN
03

Feathers & fans

Select the bones you want to affect. Inflate spreads them apart; hold Ctrl to pull them together. Refine with Twist and use masks to protect finished areas.

INFLATE → TWIST → MASK

These are suggested workflows, not automatic rig setups. BoneSculpt edits pose bones; it does not create a rig or replace its constraints.

08 / From ZIP to first stroke

Open Blender.
Find your first pose.

Version 0.13.0 requires Blender 5.0 or newer.
No extra Python packages or icon downloads.

  1. 01 / INSTALL

    Keep the ZIP zipped.

    Exit sculpting and disable any older or other BoneSculpt edition. Go to Edit → Preferences → Add-ons → menu → Install from Disk and select bone_sculpt_pro-0.13.0.zip.

  2. 02 / ENABLE

    Make it part of Blender.

    Search for BoneSculpt PRO and enable it. Clear “Enabled Add-ons Only” if it is hidden. Save Preferences if automatic saving is off.

  3. 03 / SCULPT

    Start with your bones.

    Select an armature, enter Pose Mode, and select bones. Press N, open BoneSculpt PRO and click Start Sculpting. Drag with the left mouse button; Esc or Enter exits.

Updating from an older PRO build?

Version 0.12.5 and earlier used the module name bone_sculpt. Disable that older entry before enabling bone_sculpt_pro. Install this add-on through Preferences → Install from Disk.

Before you sculpt

Know your rig.

Use pose bones with transforms the rig allows you to edit. Results depend on the armature, locks, constraints and drivers.

Locks & connected bones

Any locked rotation axis prevents brush rotation on that bone; any locked location axis prevents brush translation. Connected bones cannot translate directly. Scale locks apply per axis.

Constraints & drivers

BoneSculpt edits pose transforms. IK, constraints or driven controls can affect the visible result. Check a copy of your rig before building a workflow around it.

Animation & Tween

Auto Key inserts keys for touched, enabled transform channels at stroke completion. Otherwise, key the edits yourself. Tween needs pose-transform animation curves in the armature’s active action.

Connected masks

Protect connected parents keeps connected ancestors from moving. If you disable it, connected masked bones can shift with their parents. Disconnect Masked Bones changes the rig’s Connected setting.

09 / A few useful answers

Before your
first stroke.

Need a hand with your setup? Contact Vikas Thakur through the seller/support link on your Superhive purchase page.

Find seller support ↗
Which Blender version do I need?

Version 0.13.0 requires Blender 5.0 or newer. Earlier listing media or text may show older compatibility information. The documented installation and control checks used Blender 5.0.1; that does not certify every rig or every later Blender version.

Does this sculpt the mesh or create a rig?

BoneSculpt PRO edits the pose transforms of an existing armature using viewport brushes. It does not create a rig, replace mesh sculpting, or provide a separate IK solver. It is useful for bone chains such as hair, tails and feathers, subject to your rig’s setup.

Can I use Standard and PRO together?

Enable only one edition at a time. They share scene settings and operator IDs. Disable the other edition or older Bone Sculpt/BoneSculpt entry before enabling the new ZIP.

What happens when I undo a stroke?

Ctrl + Z and Ctrl + Shift + Z undo and redo completed strokes and their Auto Key edits while retaining the current brush selection, remembered values, channels, axes and tool controls. Bone transforms, animation keys and the actual bone masks remain undoable scene edits.

Why isn’t a brush moving my bones?

Check Pose Mode, selected/visible scope, masks, enabled transform channels and bone-local axes. Brush rotation is skipped when any rotation axis is locked; connected bones cannot translate directly. Twist and Smooth need Rotation. Constraints and drivers can also determine the final visible pose.

What should I save before using onion skin?

Keyframe other unkeyed animated edits before enabling or refreshing ghosts. Onion sampling restores this rig’s pose-bone transforms, but object transforms, custom rig-control properties and shape-key values may reset to their keyed values. Disabling Auto Update does not remove the limitation when you refresh.

Where do I get help or check the current price?

Use the BoneSculpt PRO product page on Superhive for current purchase options. For customer support, contact Vikas Thakur through the seller/support link on the page where you purchased your edition. Include the add-on and Blender versions, operating system, reproduction steps, and any error or crash report. A small example scene with private assets removed can help.
